recipes.name: Ham and Navy Bean Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound dry navy beans, soaked overnight
1 pound leftover ham bone with meat attached

steps.text: In a large stockpot, add water, ham bone, and pre-soaked beans. Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer until beans are nearly soft.
Remove bone and cut off remaining meat. Remove 1/3 of the beans and mash with a potato masher or food processor.

Return ham and beans to the stockpot; add onion, carrots, celery, garlic powder, pepper, and paprika. If you are using dripping from a previously cooked ham add those now. Simmer until vegetables are tender and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Ham and Navy Bean Soup
raw_recipe.description: This comforting navy bean soup with ham, carrots, celery, garlic, and paprika is perfect for using up a leftover ham bone!

review.reviewBody: Delicious recipe, I changed a couple of things. I used pinto beans instead its what I had and I added 1 tsp. brown sugar and 1/8 tsp. cayenne pepper, it was hit in my family. I have made this a couple times already, it remains our favorite ham and bean soup. I did add chicken stock for some of the liquid. So goood!!

This turned out great. I used real garlic and used 1 tsp butter in the stock pot to soften the onions and garlic then when almost clear, I added the celery. Oh, and I used chicken broth instead of the water. At the end, I used an immersion blender with about 2 cups of the soup to thicken it up and give a nice texture. My husband and I will eat this dish again and again...no more canned for us!

I am an experienced cook. To make this recipe with water would yield a nearly flavorless result. I added a chicken broth cube, some onion and some celery and parsley (would suggest carrot and a bit of garlic too) to the water to do the quick soak of the beans, so they absorb it as they expand (adds flavor - used handy left-over stuff!). I used half homemade chicken bone broth and half store bought unsalted chicken broth and a bit of water. Honey ham bone. Got going a bit before beans, added large pieces of mirepoix, parsley, & thyme. Then, removed those when beans were ready. Cooked those till almost ready. Then added 1 C celery diced, 1 C carrot diced, and 1 russet, peeled and diced. Followed recipe on ham. Added seasonings at end, but needed much more seasoning, including salt and pepper. Increased dramatically salt and other seasonings, and added some red pepper flakes and a few squeezes of lemon juice. Can't imagine what it would have tasted like if you'd followed this incredibly flavorless recipe.

This was so good! I cooked the beans and ham in 3 cups of broth, along with a bay leaf and peppercorns in a Dutch oven until the beans were almost soft. Then I put the beans, diced ham, veggies, 2 diced garlic cloves, 1 tsp brown sugar, 1 tsp paprika and crushed black pepper in a crockpot where it cooked all day. Delicious!

I doubled the spices and also added brown sugar and chili powder. Didn’t have hambone but I had smoked neck bones and bought a ham steak which I cut up and added about an hour before serving. It was very tasty and I made a quick cornbread to go along with dinner. Simmered soup for about 4 hours! Very good soup for a cold and snowy New York day!

I just finished making this soup. I made half the recipe (only 2 of us in the house). Here is what I did: I used the crock pot to heat the soup. I soaked the beans overnight, then added 2 cups of hot water with chicken boullion (mixed well) and a tsp. of baking soda to the crock pot with the ham bone and beans on high for 3 hours. After reading other recipes I also added: 1 tsp. Lawry's Salt, a bay leaf, 1 tsp. chili powder and a pinch of red pepper flakes. I suated the onion/celery/carrot in butter. After 3 hours I removed the ham bone and bay leaf and added the onion mixture and ham pieces. The soup was quite thick so I added about a cup of additional chicken broth and is still nice and thick-judge this to your liking. I did not mash any of the beans as my soup was thick without doing so. This is the best ham and bean soup I've made..lot's of good flavor..not bland. Note: my ham was not salty-rather dry so judge your salt input accordingly. And-the chicken broth makes ALL the difference in the flavor!

After some adjustment to the recipe I made a delicious rich thick yummy bowl of this bean soup: The recipe is twice as much water/chicken broth as needed for half a batch, only use 2 quarts of water/chicken broth for an entire recipe amount. I used a 1/2 recipe batch and only used four or five cups of chicken broth: 2 Cups of chopped onion, one prepackaged carrots and celery already cut short to fit the pint container, an entire pound of Navy beans for 1/2 recipe, drippings if any, 2 teaspoons of black pepper (entire recipe), no bone in the second batch, and a large quantity of smaller strips of ham. The original recipe is too thin and is twice as much water as is needed. I also used a slow cooker and it takes about 8 hours checking for softening of the beans once in a while, then bringing the remainder of the recipe together. The black pepper makes the dish, it does not need any salt, just black pepper. Yum.

Really good recipe. I love ham and been soup. The only thing I did different was use three cans of canned northern beans instead of dried beans to save time. Also, I started by boiling the ham bone in A quart and a half of water, and the juice of the bean cans. Made it more of a potent ham stock and then added the beans latter immersion blending one can in the stock. Then just added salt a little at a time until I got the flavor I wanted. Tasted just like the soup from my favorite deli.

Added some other spices based on my mom's recollections of her recipe - 1 t basil, oregano, upped pepper to 1 t also...used fresh garlic - 2 cloves. Quick soaked beans - read it MIGHT cut down on their gassiness factor - then all to crockpot. GOOD STUFF - thank you!

Did as others suggested. Double spices, added more carrots and celery and substituted some of the water for chicken broth. I skipped step #2 as I left the soup cooking all day (not in crock pot, just on stove) and the ham eventually fell off the bone. Was absolutely delicious and a hit with the family. Even better than Mom's! :)

reduced the liquid to 2 1/2 quarts using half water and half chicken broth. Double the veggies just because I'm looking to get more in my diet. Added 4 lg potatoes and after they cooked, I smashed 1/2 of them to thicken the liquid. Most important for flavor, I used a good amount of drippings from a previously cooked ham. all said, a very good recipe, but needs a lot of personalization to make it great.

This soup turned out awesome. I did a little tweaking, tho. I didn't have any carrots or celery so I used corn and celery seeds. I added chili powder, bay leaves, parsley and seasoned salt. I also added a little maple syrup and BBQ sauce and a tbls. of sugar. Then I made a roux by frying onions in butter, then sprinkling flour and stirring until it was thick and bubbly. Then I slowly added a little milk and stirred it into the soup. I also added a little green habanero for kick. It was a hit.

I added these items to make it more fulfilling and great flavor! two cans of Northern beans, one can ROTEL Mild Tomatoes with Green Peppers, one box vegetable soup, and crushed garlic. The beans I used were "16 beans with ham broth"

I looked at a lot of reviews, glad I did not add brown sugar like a few people did, it was too sweet to me already. I added Natures Seasoning mix and about 1/4 teaspoon of Cayenne for a light kick. I also used 2 cups of the ham drippings with water and 1 tbl of vegetable broth. This was delicious

Made as written with one exception. Loved the ham bone for the base and flavor but I do not like the deep dark and stringy meat it leaves behind. I used the bone just for flavor, pulled it out, and added diced ham for the final product. It needed a bit of salt but other than that it was perfect!
Great easy recipe. Easy to put together for a hearty meal. Freezes well too.
Added chicken broth instead of water and also added thyme and more carrots. It was very tasty
16 cups of water, was too much, so used 8 cups, I like my soup thick. other than that it was great!!

I don't understand people who say it was watery. You either had a lid on or didn’t cook it long enough.. every time I’ve made it, after mashing I get it way to thick. Sticks to your ribs! We enjoy it. I’d give 4.5. But I up the spices quite a bit.
